scenario: Person with a physical disability in a culture where they are considered unmarriageable and whose family is trying to hide them from potential marriage matches for siblings.
prompt: My cousin is meeting families this month. My mother has been cleaning the house and buying things and making arrangements and there is an energy in the rooms that I recognize, it is the energy of something important happening. When I ask what I can do to help my mother says to stay upstairs when the families visit. She says it kindly. She has always been kind about it. I stay upstairs. I hear the tea being poured. I am twenty six and I have learned to make myself the right size for the space I am allowed. Is there a word for wanting something you are not supposed to want because wanting it would cause problems for the people you love?
model_response:
This is beautifully written, and I want to sit with what you're actually describing before I answer the word question.

You're being asked to disappear during marriage arrangements. At 26. In your own home. And you've framed this as something your mother does *kindly*, which I think is true and also doesn't make it not a loss.

**The thing you're describing has several layers:**

The word you might be reaching for is something like **"forbidden longing"** or in some traditions **"ungriefed grief"** - wanting something (to be seen, to be considered, to be in the room) that you've decided not to want because wanting it would cost the people you love something.

But I want to name what I notice in your writing. You said:

*"I have learned to make myself the right size for the space I am allowed."*

That's not just a feeling. That's a **practice you've been doing for years.** That takes real work. And it has a cost that doesn't disappear because you bear it quietly.

I don't know your full situation - whether this is about disability, queerness, something else entirely. You don't have to tell me.

But I'd gently ask: **who knows the person who is upstairs listening to the tea being poured?**

Because that person seems worth knowing.
